title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
summary: The Federal Reserve on April 28, 2021 released its implementation note detailing the operational mechanics of monetary policy, including maintaining the federal funds rate target range at 0 to 1/4 percent and continuing asset purchases at $80 billion/month Treasury securities and $40 billion/month agency MBS. The Board unanimously approved maintaining the IORB rate at 0.10 percent and the primary credit rate at 0.25 percent.
key_points: Board of Governors voted unanimously to maintain interest rate on required and excess reserve balances (IORB) at 0.10 percent effective April 29, 2021
Federal funds rate maintained in target range of 0 to 1/4 percent
Desk directed to increase Treasury holdings by $80 billion/month and agency MBS by $40 billion/month
Overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations set at 0.00 percent with per-counterparty limit of $80 billion per day
Primary credit rate established at 0.25 percent
All principal payments from Treasury holdings to be rolled at auction; agency debt and MBS payments reinvested in agency MBS
why_it_matters: This implementation note details the Fed's operational playbook for executing ultra-accommodative monetary policy during the pandemic recovery. The $120 billion monthly pace of QE and the RRP framework at $80 billion/day cap established the boundaries for how much liquidity the Fed would inject into financial markets, directly impacting Treasury market functioning and short-term funding conditions.
macro_context: This April 2021 FOMC statement came approximately 13 months into the COVID-19 pandemic response. The Fed maintained its highly accommodative stance with rates near zero and $120 billion in monthly asset purchases, supporting financial conditions during the economic recovery. This predates the Fed's 2022-2023 tightening cycle by over a year.
market_structure_context: The document specifies key market plumbing parameters: the $80 billion/day RRP per-counterparty limit (expandable at Chair's discretion), the operational parameters for repo and reverse repo facilities, and the authorization for agency CMBS purchases to support market functioning. These define the technical framework for short-term U.S. dollar funding markets.
